Old Fashioned Beef Stew

Tender chunks of beef chuck braised low and slow with carrots, potatoes, garlic, and fresh rosemary in a rich savory broth.

Nothing comforts the soul on a freezing winter evening like a heavy Dutch oven simmering with beef stew. I learned this recipe during my five winters living off-grid in Montana.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs beef chuck roast, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
  • 4 large carrots, peeled and sliced thick
  • 1 lb baby yellow potatoes, halved
  • 1 yellow onion, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 4 cups beef broth
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 0.5 tsp black pepper

Cooking Instructions

  1. Toss beef cubes with salt, pepper, and flour until well coated.
  2. Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef cubes on all sides in batches, then transfer to a plate.
  3. Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot; cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
  4. Stir in tomato paste and beef broth, scraping up browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
  5. Return beef to the pot, add rosemary sprigs, cover, and simmer on low for 1 hour 30 minutes.
  6. Add carrots and halved potatoes; cover and simmer for an additional 45 minutes until vegetables are fork-tender and stew has thickened.
  7. Discard rosemary sprigs, taste for seasoning, and serve hot with crusty sourdough bread.
